Don't be precious, product development is a team sport - Ross Pearce, Callaghan Innovation

What's the toughest part of product development? 🤔✏️

We recently sat down with our Innovation and Design Specialist Ross Pearce to discuss some of the common hurdles businesses face when generating new products. One of the key failings Ross observes is becoming too precious about the thing you're working on. Passion is a great start, but is it enough to bring your idea to market successfully?

💡 We've put together a collection of free resources designed to empower Kiwi businesses on their path to success. Explore Product360 for the full suite of expert tips, advice and strategies to bring your innovation to life.

Uike Lea faka-Tonga 2023 -  Embracing Lea Faka-Tonga Daily

🌺 Cherishing Our Tongan Identity: Embracing Lea Faka-Tonga Daily 🌺
Lea Faka-Tonga is our precious heritage, a koloa (treasure) we're passing on to our children, family, and friends. It's woven into our Tongan identity and should be learned and used every day. 🗣
💬 We teach our kids through prayer, monomono making, and talanoa

Listen to Mrs Kolovula Murphy, 2021 Tonga Language Week Champion, who reminds us of the beauty of our heritage, passed on with love. ❤
Check out the video to see how we can continue sustaining and embracing Lea Faka-Tonga every day.

#TLW23
mpp.govt.nz/Tonga23

Uike Lea faka-Tonga 2023 - Message of the Day from Dr Melenaite Taumoefolau

Dr Melenaite, 2021 Tonga Language Week Champion, explores the meaning of this year's theme, which is the Tongan language will last forever if it is spoken often at home, in church, and in the community. 
Here is an English translation of Dr Melenaite's message:
"I encourage Tongan parents, caregivers, church leaders, pastors, and Sunday school teachers, indeed all Tongans to speak Tongan at home, in church, and in the community. I explain that although the majority of NZ-born children and youth are losing aspects of the Tongan Language, there is a minority who speak the language very well, and that is because their parents and caregivers speak to them in Tongan at home. I encourage Tongans to do what those parents and families do - use Tongan at home so that their children grow up to be bilingual in Tongan and English."

mpp.govt.nz/Tonga23

Uike Lea faka-Tonga 2023 - Tau'olunga of the day

Step into the world of Tongan traditions through the eyes of our little ones. The tau'olunga, a dance deeply rooted in Tongan culture, comes alive today in a truly special way. 😍
Meet the talented children from Akoteu Kato Kakala Early Childhood Education Centre, who are performing their tau'olunga to celebrate Tonga Language Week.

Tongan Language Week 2023 Theme Audio

The theme for Uike Lea Faka-Tonga 2023 is 'E tu'uloa 'a e Lea faka-Tongá 'o ka lea'aki 'i 'api, siasí (lotú), mo e nofo-'a-kāingá, which means the Tongan Language will be sustainable if used at home, church and in the wider community. 

Listen to this short audio to hear how the theme for Uike Lea Faka-Tonga 2023 is pronounced.

Kia Kaha te Reo Māori

Today marks the start of Te Wiki o te Reo Māori (Māori Language Week). The purpose of this week is to encourage the use of Aotearoa New Zealand's first official language, Māori language. Here are a few messages from our UCOL Te Pūkenga whānau to celebrate.

Megan Woods - History Homecoming

Hon Dr Megan Woods has been the Member of Parliament for Wigram since 2011. Megan is currently the Minister of Housing, Minister for Infrastructure, Minister of Energy and Resources, Minister for Building and Construction, as well as the Associate Minister of Finance. Megan has also held the ministerial portfolios for Greater Christchurch Regeneration, and Research, Science and Innovation. Prior to becoming a Member of Parliament, Megan worked as a Business Manager at Plant and Food Research.
